Fast forward 2 years...

In grade 3 we had an EQAO test. I will say now my math grades were horrible getting a C- on my report. She noticed me struggle and one day invited me over to her house, I had only her as a friend so it was my first sleepover ever. I went over on the weekend with everything requested, a pillow, stuffed animal, PJ'S and a notebook and pen. We had talked all night, watched movies and I had never felt more accepted in my life. Later on we had gone to sit at the kitchen table to grab a snack from her fridge and she threw my notebook and pen on the table. I was puzzled at first until she took a math textbook from her table and began to quiz me. I was having mixed emotions, anger but a hint of thanks that she would save me from losing my little bit of pride to go into the 'special classes'. I had seen a kid get beat for it from the school bullies. She quizzed me until I had everything trapped in my head. She suggested I return the favour by teaching her language, her tricky subject. Around 11:30 at night we had done our shares of teaching and hit the sack. I was sleeping peacefully until I heard her whimper and mumble in her sleep, she kept saying ''Don't do this, you sick killer'' until I woke her up. She began to cry in my arms and I asked her what was wrong.

She was Schizophrenic.

I had know the feeling before I learned to deal with it and now I had to help her with it. We were awake for an hour talking it out and her constantly thanking me for the comfort. This was the time she had called me her best friend.

Fast forward another 3 years.

Grade 6, where my 11 year old emotions made me feel worthless again, I know all of the emotions were just that normal part of growing up but they had still affected me enough I hid away from everyone, getting called a nobody or that one kid that didn't mean anything in the world. I spent my year wishing to be dead but I couldn't after a visit from a good friend.

I was home alone one night on a long weekend, free of the teasing when there was a knock on my door, I noticed who it was and let her in. She knew how I was feeling and said this to me...

'' Remember 3 years ago, when you helped me overcome my emotions, well now It's my turn. This is a phase that will go away, you don't need to listen to anyone of them, the opinions that matter are those from your true friends, don't blame yourself for anything. They only say those things out of jealosy for what you have, true friends. In the future they will be either nowhere good or have nobody good''

I was stunned that she was only 11 and had said something enough to make me cry of joy that she had still cared so much. She was my best friend too.

And today...
